rejected.title: The gut-brain axis
card: The gut-brain axis is the two-way link between the gut and the brain. Signals travel from the brain to the gut and from the gut to the brain.
One route is the vagus nerve, a long nerve that carries messages between the brain and the gut. The other involves gut microbes, the billions of tiny organisms that live in the gut.
Stress can change the mix of gut microbes. The brain's stress response can also affect how the gut works.
Gut health can affect mood. Changes in gut microbes may alter the signals sent to the brain, which can influence how a person feels.
rejected.remember: Signals run both ways between gut and brain, so stress can affect the gut and the gut can affect mood.

a.q: Why is the link between the gut and the brain called an axis?
opts: Signals travel both ways between the two
Signals travel only from the brain to the gut
Signals travel only from the gut to the brain
The gut and brain share the same nerve cells
a.why: An axis here means a two-way link. The brain sends signals to the gut and the gut sends signals to the brain. The option with only brain to gut is tempting because stress starts in the brain, but the card says signals also travel from the gut.
a.clue: Think about which direction the messages can go.

b.q: Lena has weeks of exam stress. Her gut microbes change, and she then feels low in mood. Which statement best explains this using the gut-brain axis?
opts: Stress changed her gut microbes, which may affect mood
Low mood changed her gut microbes, which caused the stress
Her vagus nerve carries signals only from gut to brain
Her gut microbes changed first, which then caused the exams
b.why: Stress can change gut microbes, and gut health can affect mood, so the link runs from stress to the gut and then to mood. The option that says low mood caused the stress reverses the order in this case, because the stress came first.
b.clue: Follow the order of events in the scenario, starting with the stress.

version.title: The gut-brain axis
card: The gut-brain axis is the two-way communication between the gut and the brain. The brain sends signals to the gut, and the gut sends signals to the brain.

One pathway is the vagus nerve, a long nerve running between the brainstem and the gut. Gut microbes, the trillions of bacteria and other microorganisms living in the gut, also send signals through chemicals they make.
Stress can change the mix of gut microbes and how the gut works, such as causing an upset stomach before a big event.
Gut health can affect mood. A change in gut microbes can change the signals reaching the brain, which may influence how a person feels.
version.remember: Brain and gut talk both ways: stress can upset the gut, and an upset gut can lower mood.

a.q: Which example shows a signal travelling from the gut to the brain?
opts: Changed gut microbes lead to a lower mood
Exam worry leads to an upset stomach
A frightening noise speeds up the heart
Stress hormones change the mix of microbes
a.why: When gut microbes change, the signals they send to the brain can change and affect mood, so the signal starts in the gut. Worry causing an upset stomach runs the other way, from brain to gut.
a.clue: Where does the change start, and where does it end up?

b.q: Mai has weeks of exam stress. Her gut microbes change, and soon after she feels low. Which explanation fits the gut-brain axis?
opts: Stress changed her microbes, which can affect mood
Her low mood came first and caused the stress
Signals can only travel from her brain to her gut
Gut microbes have no link to how a person feels
b.why: Stress can change gut microbes, and the changed microbes can alter the signals reaching the brain and affect mood. Signals travel both ways along the axis, not only from brain to gut.
b.clue: Follow the order of events, starting with the stress.

a.best: Changed gut microbes lead to a lower mood

b.best: Stress changed her microbes, which can affect mood

problems.detail: The stem already gives the whole chain (stress, then changed microbes, then low mood), and the right option restates it, while two wrong options contradict the stem outright. A Year 12 student can answer without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The facts and both answers are right. Question b is too easy, because its right option repeats the order of events the stem gives.

a.why: When gut microbes change, the signals they send to the brain can change and affect mood, so the signal starts in the gut. Worry causing an upset stomach runs the other way, from brain to gut.

b.q: In an experiment, calm mice are given gut microbes taken from stressed mice. Afterwards, the calm mice act more anxious. What does this suggest?
opts: Gut microbes can send signals that affect the brain
The mice's anxiety came first and changed their microbes
Signals in the axis travel only from the brain to the gut
The vagus nerve is the only link between gut and brain
b.why: The mice were calm until their gut microbes changed, so the change started in the gut and then affected behaviour. This shows signals can travel from gut to brain. The anxiety could not have come first, because the mice were calm before they got the new microbes.
b.clue: Which changed first in the calm mice, their gut or their behaviour?
